cohort: 769 live singleton births at a tertiary care teaching hospital in Lalitpur, Nepal, between April 14, 2013, and April 13, 2014 (684 neonates included in analysis: 93 macrosomic and 591 appropriate for gestational age)
finding: Macrosomic births were associated with a higher rate of neonatal sepsis (14% vs. 5.9%) and longer hospital admissions compared to appropriate for gestational age births.
mod_finding: Mothers of macrosomic babies were more likely to have a cesarean section (55.9%) compared to mothers of appropriate for gestational age babies (29.9%).
followup_time: The duration of hospital admission (not specified numerically)
birth_weight: Macrosomic (birth weight > 4000g) vs. appropriate for gestational age
